name: tabular_stacking_oof
title: A four-model stack blended out-of-fold, spelled twice: cross_val_predict by hand and StackingClassifier(cv=folds)
origin: hardening round 2, tester domain-tabular: the stacking / OOF-blending false-positive trap

forbidden.why: every fit in this file is on train_x/train_y or on the out-of-fold matrix derived from them: meta.fit at line 62, member.fit at line 66 and stack.fit at line 88 all run after the split at line 44, and each member is a Pipeline that carries its own imputer and scaler
models.py only constructs pipelines and the stack; it calls fit on nothing
test_x reaches predict_proba at lines 72 and 89 and nothing else; no transformer, member or meta learner is ever fitted on it
no split exists in models.py, so no value there can carry VAL_SPLIT or TEST_SPLIT

the estimator handed to cross_val_predict at line 53 is a make_pipeline whose first two steps are the imputer and the scaler, so every fold refits them - which is exactly the fix MLV103 asks for; the same is true of the StackingClassifier, whose members are pipelines and whose cv= is the same StratifiedKFold
no CV call exists in models.py
there is no timestamp anywhere in this project: no parse_dates, no to_datetime, no sort by a date column
the only metrics are roc_auc_score and log_loss, both in the score-metric carve-out, and both are fed a probability column
both roc_auc_score calls are fed predict_proba columns - manual_scores from line 74 and stack_scores from line 89 - never predict()
seed_everything() seeds random and numpy at lines 32-33, the split and the StratifiedKFold carry random_state=SEED, and every estimator that has one carries random_state=SEED
train_test_split at line 44 and StratifiedKFold at line 82 both pass random_state=SEED
there is no torch in this project and no hand-written gradient step
model.eval() is a torch idiom with no sklearn equivalent
torch.no_grad() has no meaning in a scikit-learn program
no device is ever named in this project

notes: The trap here is the in-sample blend, which this file deliberately does NOT do: a meta learner fitted on predictions the base learners made about rows they were themselves fitted on. There is no rule for it, so the correct shape - cross_val_predict at line 53 and StackingClassifier(cv=folds) at line 88 - cannot be scored; it is recorded so a future rule has a negative to be tested against.

member.fit at line 66 refits each base learner on the whole training half AFTER the out-of-fold matrix has been built. That is correct and is the documented sklearn behaviour of StackingClassifier itself; a rule that reads `fit on all of train_x after a cross_val_predict on train_x` as a leak would fire here.
